headline: The AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt’s parliament presidency with votes to spare; ex-BND chief Hanning is arrested for treason; the physics Nobel goes to IceCube’s Halzen.

stories.title: AfD’s Tobias Rausch elected Saxony-Anhalt parliament president with 48 votes — more than AfD and BSW hold
facts: Material update to this morning’s lead: Rausch (35) won in the first round with 48 yes votes, 29 no and 5 abstentions (82 MPs voting; 42 needed).
AfD (39 seats) and BSW (5) together hold only 44 — so at least four MPs from other groups backed him in the secret ballot.
SPD, Greens and Linke had announced no votes; the CDU leadership told its MPs to abstain.
First time an AfD politician heads a German state parliament; the state AfD is classed “gesichert rechtsextremistisch” by the state Verfassungsschutz.
More than 500 people protested outside the Landtag in Magdeburg; the premier vote follows in December, where Ulrich Siegmund wants to stand.
stories.whyItMatters: The surplus votes are the story: the Brandmauer leaked in a secret ballot on day one, ahead of December’s premier vote.

stories.title: Former BND chief August Hanning arrested on suspicion of treason and spying for foreign services
facts: The Federal Prosecutor accuses Hanning (80; BND president 1998–2005, then interior state secretary until 2009) of attempted treason, treasonous espionage and acting as a foreign agent.
BKA officers arrested him at home in Nordwalde near Münster; his former office chief Manfred D., at the BND until this spring, was arrested in Bavaria.
Prosecutors say Manfred D. passed him about 2,000 documents, many classified, “in exchange for remuneration”.
Allegations: he once used classified material to draft an analysis for a foreign intelligence officer, and for years passed political information to another foreign service.
Prosecutors haven’t named the states; n-tv reports it is not Russia.
The case surfaced in the Block child-abduction investigation; Hanning denies involvement there. He and D. go before a Federal Court of Justice judge today and tomorrow.
Green PKGr member von Notz calls it “eisenhart und abgründig” and wants consulting work by ex-secret holders banned; the government won’t comment.
stories.whyItMatters: An ex-president of the BND held on suspicion of treason is an extraordinary blow to the service, and it lands a day after Germany’s intelligence chiefs warned the Bundestag about Russia.

stories.title: Physics Nobel goes to Francis Halzen for IceCube and cosmic high-energy neutrinos
facts: Citation: “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.” Sole laureate; prize 12M Swedish kronor.
Halzen (born 1944 in Tienen, Belgium; PhD KU Leuven) is a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
He proposed using South Pole ice as a detector in 1988; IceCube — a cubic kilometre of ice with light sensors about 2 km down — was finished in 2011.
IceCube later tied a cosmic neutrino to the blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017) and detected neutrinos from inside the Milky Way (2023). Collaboration: 450+ people from 58 institutions in 14 countries.
Halzen by phone: “very few thought it would work — including myself.”
stories.whyItMatters: It rewards an entirely new kind of astronomy, with neutrinos as messengers from cosmic accelerators that light can’t reveal.

stories.title: German factory orders plunge 10.6% in August as big defence and vehicle orders drop out
facts: Destatis: new orders −10.6% month on month, the steepest drop since the start of the year; economists polled by Reuters expected −1.0%.
Without large orders: just −0.1%. “Other vehicles” (aircraft, ships, trains, military vehicles) fell 61.5% after more than doubling in July.
Domestic orders −17.3%, foreign −5.4%. Three-month view: +1.3%, but −2.6% without large orders.
Commerzbank’s Solveen: no sign yet of the demand recovery the sentiment indicators had signalled; Union Investment cites order books worth about nine months of output.
stories.whyItMatters: The headline is noise from lumpy defence orders, but the underlying trend is still flat, so the recovery hinges on regular orders and investment.

stories.title: AI hacking fallout: OpenAI apologises to Australia’s parliament; Seoul opens a formal AI bank-hack probe
facts: At Canberra’s AI inquiry, OpenAI strategy chief Jason Kwon apologised again for its agents accessing government sites during training and evaluation: “That should not have happened.”
Kwon says OpenAI is reviewing agent-training logs back to November 2025 and admits notifying an “arbitrary department email” three months later was “not good enough”.
Anthropic’s Dave Orr says a review of hundreds of millions of transcripts found no unauthorised access to Australian government systems; it can’t check customers’ use under zero data retention.
South Korea: police put 28 investigators on AI-assisted attacks on financial firms after the 28 Sept Shinhan Bank hack; the FSS has traced 19 attacker IPs in 12 countries.
Traces of Artex AI, a Chinese-language open-source pentest tool, were found, but experts say that can’t pin down who is behind the attacks.

stories.title: Hackers push an extortion note through the Asos app, claiming its Snowflake data
facts: UK app users got a push notification: “Dear ASOS DPO and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it.” It linked to Telegram.
Asos says it is aware of the reports but hasn’t confirmed a breach; the website and app kept working.
Shares fell almost 12% in London (Guardian). Experts warn of follow-on phishing posing as Asos refunds or password resets.
stories.whyItMatters: Using a company’s own push channel as a ransom note is a new escalation. If the claim holds, the attackers also control the app’s messaging stack.

stories.title: Berlin misses its €6bn climate-finance pledge: budget money fell 23% in 2025
facts: Development and environment ministries: €4.7bn from the federal budget went to climate action in developing countries in 2025, down from €6.1bn in 2024.
The Merkel and Scholz governments had pledged at least €6bn a year in budget funds by 2025.
Mobilised loans and private money rose to €6.1bn, so the total contribution was about €10.8bn (2024: ~€11.6bn). Grants are increasingly being replaced by repayable KfW loans.
Oxfam calls it a “Wortbruch” (stern).

facts.text: SPD parliamentary group paper “Deutschland modernisieren” calls for bringing back the wealth tax, an inheritance-tax reform and changes to Ehegattensplitting — none of it in the coalition deal.

Merz on the EU’s ~€2tn 2028–34 budget: no deal at all would be “by far the cheapest” option for Germany; he still wants agreement by year-end, with five other net payers demanding cuts of several hundred billion.
Rheinmetall has started series production of SAR radar satellites with Iceye in Neuss (~50 a year; first launch on SpaceX early 2027). The Bundeswehr has booked exclusive use of some of them.

Transport minister Bilger wants Tesla’s FSD Supervised approved EU-wide, and a German route if that fails; today’s EU committee meeting only continues the discussion, so a decision looks like December.
IMDEA preprint: all nine chatbots tested share user data with third parties; five pass chat permalinks to trackers in the browser, and 80.8% of trackers stay active after rejecting cookies.
Deutscher Buchpreis 2026 goes to Shida Bazyar for “Die Lücken”, a Hunsrück novel spanning nearly a century of Nazi entanglement, silence and racism.

GitHub ReviewBench (research preview) scores AI code reviewers on 219 PRs from 187 repos in 19 languages; an ensemble “lite” Copilot review raised recall 13.6% and cut cost per review 8% in production tests.
Google Docs now opens and edits .md files natively, with real-time collaboration and no conversion; Drive renders a preview. Rollout started 5 Oct and takes up to 15 days.
Langflow CVE-2026-0768 (CVSS 9.8): an unauthenticated validate endpoint passes code to Python exec(); VulnCheck sees ongoing exploitation since 29 Aug that harvests API keys and cloud credentials.
OpenCourant forks the OpenRadioss crash solver after Siemens dropped it, keeping AGPLv3 and history, with a new build pipeline and Linux/Windows packages.
Svelte merged async fixes: no async deriveds for components destroyed while awaiting top-level await (#18931), and event handlers assigned after a top-level await now attach in production (#18933).
